# ShockGuard – CAD Assembly Notes

**Status:** proposed engineering concept, Rev A. **Not validated. Not for clinical use or human testing.**
**Source:** `CAD/ShockGuard_Assembly.FCStd` (FreeCAD 1.1.4), generated by `scripts/build_shockguard.py`.
**Reference:** `ShockGuard_Vishwakarma_Proposal.docx`. The proposal fixes the architecture: a fixed-compression spring plunger, cocked by the operator and released by a single button, with no motor; a camera and ring light; MAX30102 PPG; ESP32-S3 on-device inference; an OLED readout; and a battery with charging. It gives **no dimensions, forces, battery specification or component part numbers**. Every number in this model is therefore an assumption or a placeholder; the `Params` spreadsheet tags each one.

---

## 1. Design concept (as modelled)

| Item | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Finger insertion | Palm-side down, along −X, through a U-shaped tunnel entered from the +X end; the fingertip stops on a domed end wall | Gives a repeatable X datum and a defined measurement zone |
| Measurement surface | Fingertip pad (pulp), 9 mm from the fingertip stop (`camera_mount_position`) | The pad is a standard CRT site, and it lets the camera view through the compressing element |
| Compression | Hollow plunger rises **from below** and presses the pulp through a **transparent contact window**. The finger reacts against the tunnel ceiling | Camera, ring LED and window share one axis, so the same skin patch is imaged on every cycle |
| Cocking | Pull the side knob (+Y) **down**. This compresses the spring, and the flange lead-in chamfer cams the latch tooth aside until it snaps over the flange | Manual and motor-free, as the proposal requires |
| Release | Press the **mechanical release button** (−Y side). The pivoting latch lever rotates about 8.6° and the tooth clears the flange; the spring drives the plunger up until it meets the pulp or hits the travel stop | Single-button release |
| End of compression | **Re-cocking** (knob down) lifts the window off the pulp. That moment is the refill start the camera times | Removes the need for an actuator to end compression. Dwell time is operator-paced (see Risks) |
| PPG | MAX30102 flush in the trough, 21 mm proximal to the plunger axis (`ppg_mount_position`), clear of moving parts | Records PPG/PPI at the same time without sitting under the plunger |
| UI | OLED in the roof plus an **electronic** push-button on top. It is mechanically and spatially separate from the release mechanism (≥ 49 mm apart in CAD) | Required separation: the UI button cannot fire the spring |
| Construction | Split shell. The **lower shell** is the chassis: mechanism bay, electronics bay, battery bay. The **upper shell** carries the roof, display, UI button, finger tunnel and reaction ceiling. 6× M2×30 screws from below | Serviceable and FDM-printable |

Coordinate frame: X runs along the finger axis, from the rear/USB-C end (0) to the finger entry (125). +Y is the cocking-knob side, −Y the release-button side, and Z points up. The origin is at the rear-bottom centre.

### Envelope (measured from the CAD shells)
- Housing **125 × 42 × 42 mm**. Overall **125 × 51 × 42.8 mm** including the knob, release button and UI cap.
- The height is **2 mm above the 25–40 mm guide** in the brief. The plunger stack under the tunnel sets it: floor 2, optical mount 2.5, spring seat 1, cocked spring 8, flange 3, travel 4, stop 2, support plate 3, trough 1.5 below the plate top, tunnel 16, roof 2. Ways to reduce it are listed in §6.

## 2. Model structure

```
ShockGuard_Assembly (App::Part)
├── Upper_Enclosure            ├── Optical_Assembly: Camera_Module, Ring_LED, Optical_Mount
├── Lower_Enclosure (grounded) ├── PPG_Assembly: MAX30102_Module, Sensor_Mount
├── Finger_Support             ├── Display_Assembly: OLED_Module, Display_Window
├── Plunger_Assembly           ├── Electronics_Assembly: ESP32_S3_Board, Charging_Board, Battery,
│   ├── Plunger_Body           │       Battery_Cover, Electronics_Tray, Camera_FPC
│   ├── Contact_Pad (window)   ├── User_Controls: Push_Button, Tactile_Switch, Button_PCB
│   ├── Compression_Spring     └── Fasteners: 32 App::Links to 4 parametric screw bodies
│   ├── Spring_Seat
│   ├── Guide (+ latch pivot lug)
│   ├── Travel_Stop
│   ├── Cocking_Feature (pin + knob)
│   ├── Release_Trigger (latch lever)
│   ├── Release_Button
│   └── Latch_Return_Spring
Params (Spreadsheet)  ·  Fastener_Library  ·  Reference_Geometry (Finger_Reference D14, datum axes)
```

- There are **29 PartDesign Bodies** and **32 fastener Links**, giving 61 solids. The device is not fused into one solid.
- Features include sketch-based pads, pockets and **revolutions** (plunger, guide, stop, seat, window, knob, buttons), a fully constrained rounded-rectangle sketch for each shell, PartDesign helices for both springs, fillets, primitive cuts and bosses, and countersinks.
- **All 17 sketches are fully constrained**, and every constraint, feature dimension and placement is an expression on `Params`.
- **Assembly relationships** are expression-driven placements rather than solver joints. Each part is modelled in assembly coordinates from the same master parameters, so alignment follows by construction: plunger, guide, stop, seat, collar and camera all share axis `x_m`, and the PPG uses `x_ppg`. The Lower_Enclosure is the grounded reference. I did not use the FreeCAD Assembly-workbench joint solver: its joints are awkward to script reliably headless, and expressions give deterministic propagation.

### Configurations (edit in `Params`, then recompute)
| `state` | Configuration | Stroke | Latch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Rest / reset: uncocked, flange on stop, spring preloaded 2 mm | 4.0 mm | rotated clear |
| **2** | **Cocked** (default): tooth over flange, window 0.8 mm below the trough | 0 | engaged |
| 3 | Released / contact. The 2.0 mm indentation is **illustrative only** | 2.8 mm | rotated clear |
| 4 | Maximum travel: flange on stop, no finger | 4.0 mm | rotated clear |

`explode = 1` gives the exploded configuration. The spring and latch-spring lengths follow the state. This is a **kinematic configuration set, not a force, impact or pressure simulation**.

## 3. Verification performed (CAD level only)

Run by `scripts/verify_and_export.py`; full data in `verification_report.json`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Solid validity | 61/61 solids valid, one solid per part, closed shells. No feature errors |
| Sketch constraint state | 17/17 fully constrained |
| Interference, all 4 states | **0 unintended overlaps** (pairwise boolean common > 0.001 mm³). The only overlaps are M2 screw threads in their pilot holes |
| Reference finger vs. device | No contact when cocked (0.8 mm clear of the window). Overlaps the plunger only in states 1, 3 and 4, which is the intended blanching indentation |
| Upper vs. lower shell | Faces touch with no overlap; the enclosure closes |
| Latch holds | Moving the cocked plunger up 0.3 mm collides with the tooth, so the latch physically blocks motion (gap 0.1 mm) |
| Travel stop | The flange touches the stop at maximum travel, and +0.3 mm collides, so the stop limits overtravel |
| Released tooth clearance | 0.17 mm to the flange OD |
| Spring space | Solid ≈ 5.6 mm < cocked 8 mm. On stop 12 mm < free 14 mm (2 mm preload keeps it captive) |
| Sliding fits (radial) | Flange/guide 0.3, tube/stop 0.3, tube/plate 0.5, spring/guide 0.3, spring/collar 0.7 mm |
| Moving parts vs. electronics/camera/FPC | Minimum 0.4 mm (latch-lever tip to the ESP32 carrier edge, different heights). Spring → FPC 2.0, spring → ring LED 2.2, plunger → camera 3.9 mm |
| Camera view cone | No obstruction in the cocked or released state. Half-angle 30° cocked; lens to skin 13 mm; about 14 mm of skin viewed (limited by the window) |
| Ring LED | LED edge at r = 6.3 mm, inside the 6.5 mm bore, so it illuminates the same patch through the window |
| PPG | Sensor face flush with the trough (0.00 mm); 30 mm from the fingertip stop; 5.75 mm from the nearest moving part |
| Assembly / service paths | Clear, sampled translations up to 60 mm: shell screws, upper shell (with display and UI), plate screws, finger-support plate, travel stop, battery cover, battery (out through the floor), electronics tray with both PCBs, cocking pin (radially), plunger |
| Design-rule checks | 13/13 pass: roof ≥ 1.5 mm, preload > 0, spring solid height, guide ≥ spring OD + 0.2, LED inside bore, tooth/tube clearance, lever below guide top, sensor mount clear of guide, plate covers PPG, OLED header clear of ESP32, battery below tray |
| Parameter propagation | Changed length 125→135, height 42→44, tunnel width 22→20, travel 4→5, PPG offset 21→23, spring 8/14→9/16. Recomputed with no errors, no invalid solids, no interference and 0 rule failures. After reverting, volumes match exactly (Δ = 0 mm³) |
| Export re-import | Assembly STEP re-imports as 61/61 valid solids. 33 component STEPs are valid single solids. All 15 printable STLs are closed solids with no non-manifold edges |
| FDM overhang (> 45°) in the recommended orientation | Upper shell 189 mm² (printed roof-down: lens-recess ledge and roof fillet near the bed), Lower shell 364 mm² (undersides of counterbored boss heads and the battery-recess roof), Guide 52, Optical mount 38 (FPC groove bridge), Sensor mount 16 mm². All other printable parts 0 |

**Design problems the checks caught and fixed during modelling:**
1. A 1.5 mm ridge where the finger crossed the lower-shell front wall. Fixed by running the trough through the wall.
2. The USB-C receptacle was trapped and the tray could not be lifted out. Fixed with an open-top slot plus a closing tongue on the upper shell.
3. The battery cable tab collided with a cover boss and blocked removal. Moved to the top of the cell.
4. Bosses exactly tangent to walls gave a non-manifold STL. They now overlap the wall.
5. The OLED PCB corner clipped the shell bosses. Display moved to x = 40.
6. A cable rib was tangent to a boss.
7. Assembly order: the knob passes through the wall slot, so the **cocking pin must be fitted last, radially, after the plunger is dropped into the guide**.

**Not performed:** force, stress, FEA, impact, optical (ray or focus) analysis, thermal, RF or tolerance-stack analysis. No material properties, spring rate, contact force, contact pressure or dwell time have been assigned.

---

## 4. Assembly sequence (verified free paths)

1. Press the heat-set inserts if used (see the note on pilot holes).
2. Fit the camera module into the optical-mount pocket with its FPC in the groove. Seat the ring LED on the collar. Screw the mount to the floor (4× M2×4 countersunk from below).
3. Fit the spring seat, then the guide over the collar. Fit the latch lever on the guide lug with an M2 pivot screw, and the latch return spring between the lever and the post.
4. Drop in the compression spring and the plunger (window bonded in its counterbore).
5. **Fit the cocking pin and knob radially through the +Y wall slot** into the flange bore.
6. Fit the travel stop (add shims to calibrate stroke), then the finger-support plate (3× M2×8 countersunk). This clamps the stack.
7. Fit the MAX30102 on its pedestal (screwed from below before the plate goes on).
8. Install the battery from below; fit the battery cover (2× M2×4 countersunk).
9. Install the electronics tray with the charger and ESP32 carrier (4× M2×5) and route the FPC and harness.
10. Fit the release button in the −Y wall, then fit the upper shell (OLED, display lens and UI switch pre-assembled) and close with 6× M2×30 from below.

## 6. Unresolved engineering risks and decisions

**Mechanism and safety (must be resolved before any human testing)**
- **Force is not fixed.** A fixed stroke and spring give a force that varies with finger thickness, pulp stiffness and where contact starts (F = k·(free − installed − stroke-at-contact)). Measure the force/stroke curve with a load cell across a finger-phantom set. Consider a force-limiting element: a soft-stop spring stack, a constant-force spring, or a load cell under the window for closed-loop timing.
- **Impact on release.** The plunger is spring-driven into the pulp with no damping, and the 0.8 mm free travel before contact means it strikes with some velocity. Assess the impact force and consider a damper (grease, viscous) or a slower release.
- **Dwell time is operator-paced.** Re-cocking ends compression. The proposal's "same fixed duration" needs either an OLED countdown with timing recorded from a latch/hall sensor, which is not modelled, or a timed mechanical release. This is an open decision.
- Pinch points: window and aperture edge, knob slot, tunnel mouth. Also accidental release (button stroke is only about 2 mm), spring retention under drop, and latch-tooth wear and fatigue in printed polymer.
- The maximum indentation if the finger is already against the ceiling is 3.2 mm (travel − rest gap). Whether that is acceptable is unknown.

**Optics and sensing**
- The 13 mm lens-to-skin distance needs a macro lens or a longer optical stack. Window glare (consider cross-polarisers), colour calibration across skin tones, and focus through the window are all unverified.
- A plunger bore that is not matte black will cause stray reflections.
- Whether distal blanching changes the proximal PPG/PPI reading must be tested. The MAX30102 is designed for direct skin contact; any cover or window is untested.

**Packaging and manufacture**
- Height is 42 mm against a 40 mm guide. Options: a shorter spring, smaller travel, a 2.5 mm tunnel trough or a 15 mm tunnel, or a side-mounted camera with a fold mirror.
- Pilot holes (Ø1.7) assume self-tapping M2 in PETG. **Heat-set inserts are recommended** for the 6 shell screws and the latch pivot.
- The 0.3 mm FDM sliding fits need a test coupon. The guide bore and plunger are better machined in POM or SLA-printed.
- The latch tooth (1.2 mm engagement, 2 mm thick) is fine FDM geometry; print it in POM or SLA.
- The upper shell is printed roof-down. The 2 mm roof fillet at the bed edge and the lens-recess ledge need care (a chamfer variant is recommended).
- Exported per-part STEP files keep assembly coordinates. Printable STLs are re-oriented and moved to the bed origin.
- RF: keep the WROOM antenna clear of the metal pivot screw and shell screws, and check the keep-out.

**Regulatory and clinical:** no part is validated for skin contact or biocompatibility. CDSCO classification, electrical safety, battery safety and cleaning/disinfection compatibility are all outstanding. CAD completeness does **not** mean production readiness or medical safety.
